Connecting the Torah’s end, “l’einei kol Yisrael,” back to its beginning, “B’reishis bara Elokim,” demands that we reveal the G-dliness within ourselves and the world, with unconditional Ahavas Yisrael as the ultimate sign that our soul’s essence has been revealed. latest.title: Likkutei Sichos: Sukkos
latest.blurb: The festival of Sukkos is named after the sukkah because it is the mitzvah that encompasses the entire person from the very start of Yom Tov, enabling us to elevate even our most ordinary activities into Divine service throughout the year. True joy comes from drawing on the infinite Source through kabbalas ol, rather than relying on our own limited capacities. The incomparable joy of Simchas Beis Hashoevah comes from transcending our usual boundaries, as even the highest human faculty—the intellect—finds its fulfillment in submitting to what lies beyond reason. The story of the Sadducean priest who denigrated the water libation and was pelted with esrogim shows how kabbalas ol gives intellect its proper foundation and allows it to reach its full potential. Without the Beis Hamikdash and its sacrificial offerings, the mitzvah to rejoice physically on Yom Tov is fulfilled through drinking wine, including on Chol HaMoed. Because ratzo is about drawing close to the divine (and happens during the auspicious time of prayer), it senses the divine inspiration from above even during the actual avodah b'koach atzmo of contemplation and love. Shuv, by contrast, is throughout the day, when there isn't this level of closeness and attachment to Elokus, therefore the divine inspiration is not felt as much. Though both ratzo and shuv are inspired from above (va'yashkem Lovon ba'boker), the outer dimension of ohr ein sof that radiates in a form of makif is sufficient to empower ratzo, which is itself the outer level of ohr ein sof. Shuv, on the other hand, is the ultimate purpose, and is thus rooted in and receives its power from the inner dimension of ohr ein sof, higher than ratzo. And being an ohr pnimi v'atzmi, in order for it to be felt internally (nirgash b'pnimiyus) requires a stronger effort of avodah b'koach atzmo to refine and be worthy of feeling this level of ohr.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 232: Eating and working for the sake of heaven refines the animal soul
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 189-190: This explains why "when the Temple is not standing, a person’s table affects atonement": The table, like the altar, offers and refines the animal soul, drawing down from the world of tohu and thereby bringing atonement. Thus a meal is like prayer in the fact that it refines the animal soul, as well as the physical elements of mineral, vegetable and animal that are consumed in a meal. This refinement of the animal soul is also achieved through our work: You refine your corner of the physical world and the animal soul when you run your business faithfully and ethically, without any deceit, as well as not allowing yourself to be overconsumed with your job, which then disturbs your ability to study Torah and pray. Especially when you do your work for the sake of heaven, intending to do a mitzvah -- give charity and study Torah in peace. Because, left on its own, the animal soul is driven by self-interest and will not hesitate to lie or steal for personal gain. As such, when a person refrains from acting unfaithfully, he is refining his animal soul. Elsewhere it is explained that prayer refines the cognitive soul -- the intelligence of the animal soul. But the refinement of the animal soul itself -- its emotions -- is through eating a meal. Yet prayer also refines the emotions; the difference is that in prayer the refinement is potential, while at a meal it is actualized.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 228: Shall He Who implants the ear not hear, shall He Who forms the eye not see?
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 186: This explains the verse shall He Who implants the ear not hear, shall He Who forms the eye not see? Why do we need a verse to tell us this obvious fact; what fool would think that G-d does not hear and see? Yet, the argument can be made that since G-d is completely beyond existence, we cannot attribute to G-d any qualities of creation. At the same time, G-d is aware of and supervises every detail of existence (whether in the form of "knowing" or "known," which is the difference between the ten revealed and the ten hidden sefiros). Therefore, the verse teaches us that even though G-d is certainly beyond existence, yet since He created the eye and the ear, He definitely has these qualities Himself, albeit in an infinitely higher exalted state. G-d's "eyes and ears" above are the angels, who are divinely appointed "supervisors." Their root in Atzilus is chochma and bina. These attributes are possible only in the Divine light (Ein Sof itself is completely beyond any qualities). But since the Divine light is encompassed in its source in Ein Sof, there are ten hidden sefirot encompassed there in a far higher and exalted (and non-existent) state. Thus, the shleimus in the light exists in the Core since the light is encompassed in the source. And in this context, we compare sunlight and the sun to creation and the Creator.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 227: Bittul from recognizing that creation does not add any shleimus to Ein Sof

In sum, there are two types of bittul of creation to the Creator, and they are opposites: The first aspect of bittul, derived from existence being entirely dependent on the divine reflection that sustains it, demonstrates a closeness and a relationship between them. The second aspect of bittul underscores that creation has no standing to add any shleimus to Ein Sof.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 226: Two elements in the bittul of creation to the Creator
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 185: This bittul of sunlight to the sun consists of two aspects: 1. The light is constantly dependent on its source, and is not an independent entity. 2. The luminary -- besides being utterly superior and of a completely higher caliber of shleimus than its reflection -- is not lacking even the mehus of the reflection's shleimus (the ten sefiros above), being that it is encompassed in the source with even more intensity than its reflection on earth. So too, the bittul of the creation to the Creator consists of two elements: 1. It is constantly dependent on its source, and is not an independent entity. 2. The source is not lacking any of the different elements of shleimus in Aby"a; it all exists in the source as light exists in the luminary.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 225: Bittul of creation is no less than the bittul of sunlight to the sun
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 185: On the other hand, the bittul of creation to the Creator is no less than the bittul of sunlight to the sun, because the creation is completely dependent on the divine energy that creates it, without which creation would not exist at all. Its entire existence is, in truth, the divine ayin that creates and sustains it. And both the divine reflection that creates existence and existence itself are encompassed in their source, and thus, do not add any shleimus to Ein Sof. This bittul of sunlight to the sun consists of two aspects: 1. The light is constantly dependent on its source, and is not an independent entity. 2. The luminary -- besides being utterly superior and of a completely higher caliber of shleimus than its reflection -- is not lacking even the shleimus of the reflection, being that it is encompassed in the source with even more intensity than its reflection on earth.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 224: Existence doesn't add shleimus to, and is infinitely distant, from the Creator
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 184-185: Two reasons why existence doesn't add any shleimus to the Creator: 1. Being in truth only a reflection of the Divine (the fact that we are created like a yesh is only from the perspective of our feeling). 2. Existence itself exists within its source (the light within Atzmus) -- in the ten hidden sefiros, as the Creator envisions existence (shi'er b'atzmo b'koach). As such, the Divine does not lack the shleimus of existence; the koach above lacks no po'el (as discussed at the beginning of the hemshech). Why then is creation a new entity called yesh m'ayin when it really exists within its source? Because after all, creation has nothing in common with its Creator, the yesh is infinitely distant from the ayin that creates it, unlike sunlight and the sun, which is yesh m'yesh.

latest.title: Samach Vav Part 222:  We invoke the angels' passion to impact the animal soul, rooted in the angels
latest.blurb: Samach Vav p. 182-183: Why do we need to invoke the angels (in the blessings before Shema) to appreciate the greatness of the Divine, especially considering that souls are greater than angels, so why do we get excited by the angels' excitement? Answer: Invoking the angels' praise and love is to impact the animal soul, which stems from these angels. The angels' excitement results from their contemplation about the source and manner of their creation (in addition to them being created from a mere reflection). This contemplation consists of the following: The Divine creation of existence is fundamentally different from a man-made creation, which essentially consists of reshaping an existing entity (yesh m'yesh), not a creation of existence from non-existence (yesh m'ayin). As such, a man-made product, though the producer applies himself to producing the product and his power manifests in the product, yet after the product is produced, it is a separate, self-contained entity and is no longer in need of the producer, since it was an existent entity (in its raw form) even before it was reshaped by the producer. Vice versa as well: The very raw matter of the product, as well as its reshaped state and the benefit and function of this newly shaped product, does not exist within the power of the producer.
